# Yoto & Growthbook Demo
Date: 2026-08-27 | Duration: 62.2400016784668m

## Summary
The discussion covered the challenges faced by the team with their current experimentation tools, which are disjointed and unstable, leading to only 1-2 experiments per month. With the contract expiring in January, there is an urgent need to explore alternatives. The engineering team expressed frustrations about integration issues and the user experience, while product leads aim to increase experiment velocity significantly. Growth Book was highlighted as a promising solution, offering a warehouse-native platform suitable for cross-platform experimentation and feature flagging. Its integrations with tools like BigQuery also ensure robust data management, while the system’s capability for family-level user attribution aligns with the company’s needs. A vendor demo is scheduled for next week to further assess Growth Book before making a recommendation to leadership.

## Keywords
experimentation platform, data warehouse native, Snowplow integration, feature flagging, cross-platform testing, AI-assisted analytics

# Yoto & GrowthBook PM Session
Date: 2026-11-09 | Duration: 62.58000183105469m

## Summary
Yoto evaluated GrowthBook as an open-source experimentation platform with paid capabilities for web, mobile, and server-side testing. Its main priorities were content ranking, recommendations, carousels, audience segmentation, and experiments for a new app home surface. PM self-service was central, including reusable metrics, experiment monitoring, segmentation, reporting, visual-editor tests, and split-URL comparisons. GrowthBook described a developer-configured SDK workflow, read-only BigQuery analysis, Snowplow exposure data, funnel measurement, Bayesian and Frequentist analysis, health monitoring, and shareable results. Yoto prefers family ID for consistent assignment, but anonymous-to-authenticated merging, app Snowplow implementation, and cross-device identity linking remain dependencies. AI, MCP, development-first validation, QA previews, approval workflows, and gradual rollouts were also discussed. Yoto was in final testing, comparing GrowthBook with one other vendor, and requested follow-up information on interleaving, QA, and approval workflows before completing scoring. (References: 06:22–01:00:50.)

## Keywords
Experimentation platform, Feature flags, Cross-platform identity, BigQuery analytics, Visual editor, Split-URL testing
